title: LockBit, 2.0 → 3.0
deck: A documentation diff of one ransomware-as-a-service lineage, built from 2022–2023 public reporting and mapped against current MITRE ATT&CK v20.0.
scope: Historical LockBit reporting from February 2022 through June 2023, mapped to LockBit 2.0 (S1199) and LockBit 3.0 (S1202) in MITRE ATT&CK v20.0, with direct evidence from FBI and CISA reporting.
universeNote: The comparison universe is deliberately narrow: the 26 and 34 techniques mapped to the two ATT&CK v20.0 software entries. Advisory-only techniques are out of the diff counts. The historical reporting period ends on 14 June 2023.

snapshots.label: LockBit 2.0
snapshots.period: Observed since at least June 2021 · snapshot 4 Feb 2022
snapshots.summary: The FBI flash describes a heavily obfuscated Windows encryptor, GPO-driven domain encryption, Stealbit exfiltration and a language exclusion check.
snapshots.limitations: The FBI flash is an IOC bulletin, not an exhaustive TTP catalogue. Some ATT&CK mappings come from vendor analysis cited by MITRE.

snapshots.label: LockBit 3.0
snapshots.period: Observed since at least June 2022 · snapshot 14 Jun 2023
snapshots.summary: The 2023 advisories document a more modular build: password-gated payloads, Safe Mode reboot, mutex checks, PsExec spreading and broader defence impairment.
snapshots.limitations: The June advisory covers LockBit affiliates broadly, not just 3.0. The March advisory is the stronger source for build-specific behaviour.

caveats: The intelligence period is February 2022 – June 2023. ATT&CK v20.0 is a current mapping layer, not evidence of activity in 2026.
Newly documented is not the same as newly adopted. A technique can appear in a later public report because reporting improved, because a new source was cited, or because the mapping was refined.
A missing public Sigma rule is not evidence that an organisation has no detection. The catalogue is small and does not represent any particular telemetry estate.
The diff compares ATT&CK software mappings, not incident prevalence. Counts describe documentation, not adversary frequency.
